paragraphs.heading: Reduce to absurdity
paragraphs.edited: We'll see a couple of strange things throughout the study, and one of those things is this weird term you see in Latin, called reductio ad absurdum. I'll say that again: reductio ad absurdum. Essentially, it's just a fancy Latin word that means reduce to absurdity. It's that simple — and even that seems kind of confusing. So let me give you an example that should help you explain this kind of strange concept to your students.

paragraphs.edited: When I was a kid, every so often I would skip school, and this one time in particular my dad caught me. So naturally he asked me, why did you skip school? I had this genius idea, this genius logic that I had come up with, and I told him, well, all my friends were doing it, so that's why I did it. That makes sense. That made perfect sense in my head, and I kind of stood there waiting for him to make a response. He didn't take very long before he said, well, if all of your friends jumped off a bridge, would you too?

paragraphs.heading: Paul reasoned from Scripture
paragraphs.edited: So take Paul, for example. If you look through Acts — whether Paul's in Corinth, whether he's in Ephesus, whether Paul's in Thessalonica or in Athens — what you see is that Paul is constantly using logic. He's reasoning from the Scriptures, helping them understand who Jesus is, what he's all about, and what salvation means. Essentially, Paul uses logic through and through in almost every single one of his arguments as he's traveling on his missionary journeys. So the idea is that we want to invite students into a space where they can be curious, where they can not only ask the questions but logically think through these things and add an intellectual piece to their faith.

paragraphs.edited: As you dive into small group, you're going to ask what looks like a really simple question: should faith make sense? That's kind of tricky, right? There's a little bit going on here that we need to address, because there's so much about Jesus that does not seem to make sense. There's so much about our faith that doesn't seem to make sense sometimes. But as we think through it, as we use logic, as we actually engage intellectually with our faith, there's a lot we can figure out, and God has given us the tools to do so.

paragraphs.heading: Sending students out

Because remember, Jesus calls us all to clear and careful thinking — the same kind of thinking that Jesus demonstrated.
